#git #git-format-patch git format-patch omits merge commits from its output by default, so it cannot directly produce a patch of a merge result.

#git #merge-commits The option --m2 (or --m<parent-number>) is NOT supported by git format-patch; using it fails with "fatal: unrecognized argument: --m2". That parent-selection style option belongs to git diff-tree / git log -m, not format-patch.

#git #merge-commits Working way to save a patch of a merge result: `git log -p -m -1 <merge-commit> > merge-commit.patch` — -p emits the patch, -m treats the merge as diffs against each parent, -1 limits to that one merge commit.

#git #merge-commits Alternative for merged changes: `git diff <parent1> <merge-commit>` (or git diff-tree -m) shows the merge result diff; patches including merges can conflict when applied elsewhere, so review before applying with git apply.
#git #git-format-patch `git format-patch A..B` produces one patch file per commit (mail-formatted, applyable with git am); `--stdout` prints instead of writing files.
